q: It seems like everyone around me either had wonderful pregnancies or very mild first-trimester symptoms. Meanwhile, I've barely been able to function.
cx: Almost 7 weeks; missed work and cancelled plans because of sickness.

q: Everywhere I look, pregnancy is portrayed as this beautiful, exciting experience, and while I am incredibly grateful and happy to be pregnant, the reality for me right now has been really difficult.
cx: Same author.

q: I couldn't go to work on Monday […] I tried going into the office on Wednesday, but I had to leave early. Since then, I've been working from home because I'm constantly dizzy and nauseous.
cx: Same author on her first week of being too sick to work.

q: I’m going to a chiropractor regularly but it feels like it’s doing next to nothing. I’m only 18 weeks and so scared for the rest of pregnancy if this is how painful it is right now.
cx: Second baby; pelvic pain came in the third trimester last time, at 18 weeks this time.

q: I’m a SAHM and trying to keep up with a 3 yr old boy. I feel guilty for giving my toddler screen time but I’m in so much pain I don’t know what to do sometimes.
cx: Same author.

q: I am losing my mind trying to take care of my very hyper active 2 year old son while feeling like I’m about to throw up every 5 minutes. I’m exhausted. I don’t know how to cope.
cx: Seven weeks with her second, Canada; many remedies already tried.

q: I’m just scared it’s going to last a long time. My first pregnancy I had only slight nausea some days, and it lasted until about 12 weeks.
cx: Same author.

q: We just bought a house to move closer to work 7 months ago. Our expenses went up drastically from doing so. […] I’ve been applying to jobs the past week in preparation and I’m already being rejected with no interview.
cx: Expects her role to go in a restructuring this month.

q: My employer does know I’m pregnant but I’m sure they will have some reason of how if I’m laid off it has nothing to do with me being pregnant.
cx: Same author.

q: So my sister had kids first. She said she focused so much on pregnancy and labor prep she didn't prep herself for postpartum at all. The amount of bleeding, healing, what to expect, how much help she would need, what moods are normal and not, etc.
cx: New mother listing what she wishes she'd prepared for.

q: So when I got pregnant, I focused on pregnancy, labor, postpartum, and like the first 3 weeks of a newborn. You know....I took classes on how to breastfeed, newborn basics like baths, how many poops and feeds are normal etc. I WISH I WOULDVE prepared for the beyond. Like 1-4 months especially.
cx: Same author; learned from her sister, still found the gap moved later.

q: I had no freaking idea what a developmental leap was. I still don't lol I wish I would've bought that Mayo clinic book and skimmed a bit of it.
cx: Same author.

q: I know we aren't supposed to know it all especially from the beginning but man I could've used a class for "How to survive when the sleepy potato baby wakes up after 2 weeks old and starts crying 24/7".
cx: Same author.

q: Thankfully school is out for the summer because I’m not ready for EVERYONE to know and I don’t feel like I can hide it!
cx: 14 weeks, already 'looks pregnant'; works at a school.

q: And imagining childbirth doesnt feel so scary. Like I just feel capable. I feel like my body is doing what it is meant to do, and I know this is insane but I feel like I am somehow good at it?
cx: Five weeks; never wanted to be pregnant, now surprised at feeling calm and fascinated.

q: I am currently off sick with pregnancy related illness and am normally receiving £245.33 every two weeks. The period of time that decides if I am eligible for SMP is 1st May - 4th July 2026.
cx: UK; a payroll error might push her average earnings under the SMP threshold.

q: on the 8th May I received a payment of £49.30 from my workplace as a one off payment […] If the £49.30 is included in the pay days then the calculator on the government website says I am not eligible for SMP as the £49.30 brings my average earnings down to under the amount needed for SMP.
cx: Same author; her reading of the government calculator, not a ruling.

q: so now I have a lot of food I only ate one meal from😩, fortunately my boyfriend eats a lot but if it keeps going like this it is going to be an expensive pregnancy.
cx: Six weeks; only one food appeals at each meal.

q: I’m 26 and I’m currently in a graduate school program and work an only a part time retail job. My husband is a teacher at the start of his career, so he’s not making a lot of money rn either, so we are a bit concerned about the financial aspect of this.
cx: Just found out, about 5 weeks; first OB visit at 8 weeks.

q: Additionally, I thought I would have more time to learn about what vitamins to take and how to take care of myself while pregnant, so any advice would be v helpful.
cx: Same author; conceived faster than expected.

q: I'm just scared, because I have my first OB appointment on Tuesday and I'm worried they're going to be upset with me.
cx: Nine weeks; scale shows a big jump since she found out.

q: ultimately determined that it’s the better thing for me to have an elective c-section, which has resulted in an endless back and forth with my doctors because apparently not all providers will accept a primary elective c-section, which like, wtf. So here I am now, at 36+5, with no clear date
cx: First pregnancy, several complications; told to deliver at 37 weeks.

q: I feel like I’ve done everything. I don’t want to get induce🫩 please I need any type of advice! how can I get her out?
cx: 39+6, a membrane sweep the day before didn't start labour.

q: the hard part is I'm 20 weeks pregnant and have not disclosed this yet. I do know their parental leave policy and luckily will qualify for it, fully paid. […] So, when do I tell them? Before signing? Right after I sign? After starting?
cx: Laid off at 5 weeks pregnant; now holding a job offer at 20 weeks.

q: if I start on June 15th, I’d only be working for a little less than 4 months before going on a 16-week leave. There isn’t a tenure requirement so I’m eligible for it right away, which is great. But I feel so guilty.
cx: Same author; her new manager planned big projects for the autumn.

q: someone told me it can come off as me giving them a way out, which I hadn’t thought of before. Even so, telling them right by after signing feels like I’m doing a bait and switch in them. It’s so tricky :(
cx: Same author on the timing of telling.

q: as I sit here having just thrown up my entire dinner, I feel less and less desire to wait. I really need something to be excited about amidst all the vomiting lol.
cx: Third pregnancy, already has a boy and a girl; tempted to open the blood-test result.

q: i had another social event tonight that i decided to cancel and the guilt has been eating me alive because i feel like im letting people down, especially my boyfriend.
cx: Seven weeks, unplanned first pregnancy; used to have a big social life.
